opex.text: The Company’s earnings are also affected by fee income from mortgage banking activities, the provision for (reversal of) credit losses, service charges and fees, gains from sales of assets, operating expenses and income taxes.

costs.text: The Company’s earnings are also affected by fee income from mortgage banking activities, the provision for (reversal of) credit losses, service charges and fees, gains from sales of assets, operating expenses and income taxes.

prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the provision for credit losses was $3.5 million, consisting of a $3.0 million provision for credit losses on loans, a $409,000 provision for credit losses on unfunded loan commitments, and a $100,000 provision for held-to-maturity investments. This compares to the provision for credit losses of $2.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, which consisted of a $1.9 million provision for credit losses on loans, a $457,000 provision for credit losses on unfunded loan commitments, and no provision for held-to-maturity investments. The increase in the provision for credit losses on loans reflects higher loan balances and increased nonaccrual loans, primarily due to the loans acquired in the Pacific West Acquisition.

nonint.text: The Company’s earnings are also affected by fee income from mortgage banking activities, the provision for (reversal of) credit losses, service charges and fees, gains from sales of assets, operating expenses and income taxes.

nonop.text: The Company’s earnings are primarily dependent upon net interest income, the difference between interest income and interest expense. Interest income is a function of the balances of loans and investments outstanding during a given period and the yield earned on these loans and investments. Interest expense is a function of the amount of deposits and borrowings outstanding during the same period and interest rates paid on these deposits and borrowings.

tax.text: Provision for Income Taxes. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a provision for income taxes of $1.2 million, compared to $2.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to lower pre-tax income. The effective corporate income tax rates for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, were 19.1% and 20.8%, respectively.

Net interest income.text: The Company’s earnings are primarily dependent upon net interest income, the difference between interest income and interest expense. Interest income is a function of the balances of loans and investments outstanding during a given period and the yield earned on these loans and investments. Interest expense is a function of the amount of deposits and borrowings outstanding during the same period and interest rates paid on these deposits and borrowings.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest Income. Noninterest income increased $582,000 to $6.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $5.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase primarily reflects the bargain purchase gain of $1.7 million from the Pacific West Acquisition, partially offset by a decrease of $971,000 in gain on sale of loans, reflecting lower volume on residential mortgage loan sales due to the current interest rate environment, and a decrease of $231,000 in other noninterest income.

intro.text: FS Bancorp, a Washington corporation, was organized in September 2011 for the purpose of becoming the holding company of 1st Security Bank upon the Bank’s conversion from a mutual to a stock savings bank (“Conversion”). The Conversion was completed on July 9, 2012. At December 31, 2025, the Company had consolidated total assets of $3.2 billion, total loans receivable, net of $2.62 billion, total deposits of $2.67 billion, and total stockholders’ equity of $307.7 million. The Company has not engaged in significant activities other than holding the stock of the Bank and providing capital to it through the debt and equity markets. Accordingly, the information set forth in this Form 10–K, including the consolidated financial statements and related data, relates primarily to the Bank.

lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
